criterion.residual_if_not: some irreducible component of G is contained in every direction-consistency conic; this is the A=386 global-component residual
criterion.safe_if: each irreducible component of G is cut by at least one direction-consistency conic
criterion.setup: in the A=386 Q-plane, let two direction-consistency conics F_1,F_2 have full common component G of degree c in {1,2}

summary.remaining_residual: an irreducible component contained in all direction-consistency conics

theorem.component_cut: If every irreducible component G_i of G is cut by some direction-consistency conic, then the total length on G is at most sum_i 2 deg(G_i)=2c.
theorem.component_decomposition: If F_1 and F_2 share a full common component G of degree c, then their common zero set is contained in G together with the intersection of the residual conics of degree 2-c.
theorem.finite_root_bound: Thus the finite Q-classes are at most 2c+(2-c)^2, which is 3 for c=1 and 4 for c=2.
theorem.off_component_bound: The residual off-component intersection has length at most (2-c)^2.
theorem.projective_safety: The split-locator gate cannot increase this finite count, and the endpoint-uniform theorem contributes one endpoint, giving total at most 5<=6.
